Either we will start at 12.20, continue until 1.30 as we had said and that the Major would come back for that part of his cross-examination which has not been completed, or we'll stop now and conduct the cross-examination on another date since there will be a right to reply on the part of the Prosecutor and then, of course, the Judges' questions as well, which means that this is going to cover quite a long period of time. I would like the Defence to choose so that there be no ambiguity.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Although we would regret losing the hour, we think it's best if we stop now and complete the witness in one piece when the time becomes available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think out of respect for Judge Shahabuddeen that would be better because that way he will have the entire transcript of the testimony which would be easier for him. And for the interpreters, I hope that this will be marked on the credit side because we're always considered debited as Judges, but I would like to hear what the Prosecutor has to say as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have heard for the duration of this trial that the Prosecutor is attempting to slow this process down. Last week, the last session we heard from Mr. Hayman informing this chamber that we should forfeit time if we didn't conclude the amount of time that we had. Now, Mr. President, we have selected witnesses in order to fill the time available to us. We would have put another witness on the stand who would have concluded his testimony, both direct and cross-examination, had we known that we were going to be given the opportunity to conclude less than at 1.30 in the afternoon. The contract that was made with the Prosecutor's office, at the insistence of the Defence, was that we needed to fill every minute of every minute available to us and we have endeavoured to do that, Mr. President. We would object and we would urge this Chamber to reconsider and permit this witness to conclude his testimony at 1.30 as we had originally scheduled.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I am all the more less inclined to say that you are right, Mr. Harmon, because I would like to point out, and when I say "you," I don't mean you specifically, Mark Harmon, but you never respect the time that you say you are going to. Mr. Cayley said he would take an hour for his examination. I noted this down. We began today at 9.45, we went until 10.15, from 10.45 until 12. So it lasted one hour and 45 minutes. I'm sorry, it was an hour and 45 minutes, 45 minutes more than had been planned. I can't do anything about that. I didn't interrupt you. I'm following step by step. Excuse me, Major, but we're at the very core of the justice which is being created here, and I have nothing to conceal, nothing at all. In public, I'm concealing nothing about what I'm doing. We have to be conscious of what we're doing. Each witness, whether it be an expert or a victim, recounts the entire time he was on the territory. If he was there for six months, he speaks about six months. That is your choice. I have nothing to say about the choice. One day I will act differently, perhaps I'll act the way President Cassese did. I would read the declaration first. I didn't do it because everything would have to be translated into French. Last night I said to the witness, "Do you confirm you state this, this, and that? You do? All right, let's move into the cross-examination right away," but I didn't. You were given a great deal of freedom. We tried to give you a framework as much as possible for the important points. I don't want to make more rulings than I have done or more than I said even before the witness came in. I asked for the essential points. You have brought out everything now that you said you were going to. We went as far as Stupni Do, everything. We started from the initial training of the witness until his work in Yugoslavia. I didn't say anything about that. I thanked the witness very, very warmly for all of what he has done for us, but I have to give equivalent rights to the cross-examination, and the cross-examination should not be cut. It also has its own unity. Don't worry, Mr. Harmon, this time will be credited to you. You will have the time but we want to take into account certain necessities. If nobody makes an effort, if nobody makes an effort, I can say to you that starting from September on, this Trial Chamber is going to set a number of hours by week which will be very precise. Either you will fit in or you won't fit into that limitation, but everybody, when he exposes the logic that he wants to follow through the various proceedings, he will do that, but the Judges also have their own logic. We have a presiding officer because Judge Shahabuddeen is not here right now. The time is not going to be counted against you but it will be advantageous for the interpreters, and I have no regrets about this because they work longer than planned. So the witness will return. Let's think about that. We are very very faltering first steps of international justice and international justice must be organised. There's no price on time, not for the Prosecution, not for the Defence, and I claim the opposite. There is a factor in justice which is time. If we had eternity, justice would be perfect but we don't have eternity. Therefore, having said this and in agreement with Judge Riad, we have decided that we would suggest going until 2.00, but at that point I would have to ask the interpreters to work another 30 minutes. I have scruples about that. I don't want to. They have the dignity of their work which is just as important as ours, I have to say that, and the cross-examination, in any case, would not be completed. I'm sorry, Mr. Cayley, and I say it to you with all the consideration that I have, for you had said that "I had planned to talk for an hour." Yesterday, I said in front of everybody that there would be the last witness brought in. And remember even as a joke, Mr. Cayley, you said that you would work for an hour and no more. We are not going to change what we said and the hearing is adjourned and we will resume on the 29th of June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: 12.13 p.m. to be reconvened on Monday, the 29th day of June, 1998 at 10.00 a.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
